pr_title: Implement Wake On Lan Dummy State
pr_body:
<!--

-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->
Wake on LAN component now assumes a dummy state if a host is not provided. Before, the state was only based on the `host` config parameter, which is listed as optional. With this change the `host` config is still optional, but if it is not defined, the state of the switch is simply the last action that was taken. If you're relying on a Wake on LAN entity in an automation or script, please check that your assumptions about state still hold.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Prior to this change, WOL listed `host` as optional in the configuration. However, the only way that the state was updated was by pinging the host that was provided. Because of this, if no host is provided, HA attempted to ping `None`, causing a lot of erroneous DNS lookups and providing an inaccurate state. This implements a `dummy_state` that will fallback to assumed state if no `host` is defined in the configuration.

issue_context.title: wake_on_lan does tons of lookups for "none" when host name is not provided
issue_context.body:
### The problem

when a `switch` using the wake_on_lan platform is defined without a host

```
- platform: wake_on_lan
  name: wakeup_acoustix
  mac: "bc-5f-f4-88-ee-ee"
```
it spams the dns server (in this case hassio_dns) with

```
[INFO] 127.0.0.1:53104 - 2639 "A IN none.local.hass.io. udp 47 true 2048" NOERROR - 0 0.000024996s
[ERROR] plugin/errors: 2 none.local.hass.io. A: plugin/forward: no next plugin found
[INFO] 172.30.32.1:56119 - 2639 "A IN none.local.hass.io. udp 36 false 512" SERVFAIL qr,rd 36 0.000611473s
[INFO] 172.30.32.1:56119 - 2639 "A IN none.local.hass.io. udp 36 false 512" SERVFAIL qr,aa,rd 36 0.000063403s
[INFO] 172.30.32.1:56119 - 2639 "A IN none.local.hass.io. udp 36 false 512" SERVFAIL qr,aa,rd 36 0.000053941s
[INFO] 172.30.32.1:56119 - 2639 "A IN none.local.hass.io. udp 36 false 512" SERVFAIL qr,aa,rd 36 0.000037666s
[INFO] 172.30.32.1:56119 - 2639 "A IN none.local.hass.io. udp 36 false 512" SERVFAIL qr,aa,rd 36 0.000034267s
[INFO] 172.30.32.1:56119 - 2639 "A IN none.local.hass.io. udp 36 false 512" SERVFAIL qr,aa,rd 36 0.000090452s
[INFO] 172.30.32.1:56119 - 2639 "A IN none.local.hass.io. udp 36 false 512" SERVFAIL qr,aa,rd 36 0.000155232s
[INFO] 172.30.32.1:56119 - 2639 "A IN none.local.hass.io. udp 36 false 512" SERVFAIL qr,aa,rd 36 0.000061433s
[INFO] 172.30.32.1:56119 - 2639 "A IN none.local.hass.io. udp 36 false 512" SERVFAIL qr,aa,rd 36 0.000139206s
[INFO] 172.30.32.1:56119 - 2639 "A IN none.local.hass.io. udp 36 false 512" SERVFAIL qr,aa,rd 36 0.000168086s
```

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.3.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

wake_on_lan

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/wake_on_lan/

### Example YAML snippet

```
switch:
  - platform: wake_on_lan
    name: wakeup_acoustix
    mac: "bc-5f-f4-88-ee-ee"
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

This seems to fix it.

```
switch:
  - platform: wake_on_lan
    name: wakeup_acoustix
    mac: "bc-5f-f4-88-ee-ee"
    host: "realhostname.domain.com"
```

wake_on_lan seems do a ping by host after, maybe to check if the host if up, but if no host is provided it pigns "none" 

I suspect the fix is here the schema/documentation needs to set such that`host` is required element.
